Resolves #19450

Related: #14800 (the v13.2 cut; the operator's hand check of `apps/workstation` found it release-blocking today), #19556 (the other defect of that check, Ada's), #15252 (the take waits on both).

A torn-out tab now opens its window at the size the pane showed at in the room, not at the tab header's proxy size (which put every vessel on Chrome's 320×240 floor). The sort zone measures the card body the dragged pane fills at drag arming — the one moment the pane is certainly laid out; the exit admission comes after the host stages it — and the exit payload carries it as `sourceRect` through `TearOut` to the host's `openVessel` seam. One engine helper, `Placement.resolveVesselSize`, sizes the vessel in OUTER window pixels: the source by default, a host-pinned `tearOutVesselSize` when the product wants one size, the popup floor below, the screen's usable area above; without a measurement the helper's fallback applies, never the header's size. `Main.windowOpen` applies those values as the window's total extent. The vessel is still born at the proxy's position, under the hand. Fleet Manager adopts the helper in its own repo, as the ticket says.

**The sizing contract (the operator, 2026-10-10):** the popup's OUTER size equals the widget's; its body is smaller by the window chrome on purpose. The header pop-out preserves the widget's on-screen footprint, and a popup larger than the widget it replaces is the unwanted outcome, so no chrome is added to keep the content area. The rationale sits beside the helper and the host's admission seam. The first head added the popup chrome to the `height` feature so the content matched the pane; Emmy's review and the operator's word removed it (a32fe43ccf).

Evidence: L3 (headless e2e + unit) → L3 required (AC-1 to AC-4); the operator's hand check at the merged head is #14800's step, not a residual of this leaf.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `DockTabSortZone.spec` pins the card snapshot at arming; `DockTearOut.spec` pins `sourceRect` on the `openVessel` payload — CI |
| AC-2 | `DockVesselSize.spec`: source size, pin over source, the floor, the screen ceiling with no chrome term, the fallback — CI |
| AC-3 | `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL` "#18409": the vessel's OUTER size equals the pane's rect within 2 px (floored) — Test Evidence |
| AC-4 | `WorkstationFilmTourNL` 3/3 with pane-sized vessels; the film pins no vessel size (its witnesses read live rects) — Test Evidence |

## Deltas from ticket
- One sharpening of step 1: `TearOut` keeps zero imports and runs without a browser, so the measurement lives in the sort zone's arming snapshot (next to the toolbar rect it already takes) and rides the exit payload; `TearOut` only passes `sourceRect` through.
- A first cut measured in the host at `openVessel` time and read an empty rect: by then the pane is staged. That is why the measurement moved to arming.
- Chrome sizes a popup's `height` feature as the frame, location bar included (a 279 px request is a 279 px outer window with 212 px of content on the operator's macOS; his park receipt shows the same 67 px). That is the contract, not a defect: the ticket's Contract Ledger (Grace, 16:30Z) and AC-3 say OUTER.

## Test Evidence
- Headless e2e at a32fe43ccf: `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL` 5/5 (the #18409 arm pins the zone's `sourceRect` at arming against the pane's bounding box, and the vessel's `outerWidth`/`outerHeight` against the pane's floored rect; no inner-size condition), `WorkstationFilmTourNL` 3/3, `WorkstationTearOutSourceContinuityNL` 3/3 — 11/11 in 2.4 min.
- The arm's pane is 220×278.5 px, so the vessel opens at 320×279 outer (width floored).
- Unit: 173/173 across `Workspace.spec`, `DockTabSortZone.spec`, `DockTearOut.spec`, `DockPlacement.spec`, `DockVesselSize.spec` — a null source gives 360×480, a 1400 px pane under 87 px of main chrome gives 1080 with nothing taken off, a pin beats the pane, the position stays the proxy's; both hooks green.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [x] The operator's hand check: a torn-out Workstation pane opens at its own outer size on his display (#14800 step 2) — confirmed 2026-10-10 17:1xZ at dev 5ccdb192d6 on a fresh worker served by the webpack dev server: the Scale pane measured 457.8×471 at arming (`lastVesselOpen.sourceRect`), the vessel opened at 458×471 outer (read over the Neural Link). His IDE's built-in server had kept serving pre-merge modules after the pull, even to a restarted SharedWorker; that, not the fix, produced the first "still 320×240" attempt.
- [ ] Fleet Manager's `VesselContainer` adopts `Placement.resolveVesselSize` (Institution, its own leaf).
